scope: packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts generates every agent's frontmatter: toolsOf/WEB/WRITING/the T3 Code inspection lists for specialists (around lines 300-391) and the root's tools line (around 416-437). Today a `tools:` allowlist names exact built-ins and exact MCP tool names, so any other MCP server never reaches an agent.

Facts from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (read 2026-10-26): omitting `tools` makes a subagent inherit every tool available to subagents, MCP tools included; `disallowedTools` is a denylist with the same format and is applied first; `Agent(type, ...)` in `tools` restricts spawnable types only for an agent running as the main thread, and a type list is ignored in a subagent definition; background subagents keep every MCP tool but only Read, Grep, Glob, LSP, Bash, PowerShell, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, Skill, ToolSearch, EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree, Monitor, TaskStop, SendMessage, Artifact among built-ins.

Decision recorded in the Intent: each agent drops its `tools:` line and gets `disallowedTools:` listing the built-in tools its current allowlist does not grant, so each role keeps exactly its present built-in capabilities (read-only roles still cannot Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/Bash where they lack it today) while inheriting all MCP tools. WebSearch and WebFetch are in every agent's denylist. The root loses the `Agent(holyagent:...)` spawn allowlist (its instruction text still names the specialists) and keeps no Edit, Write or NotebookEdit. The explicit Exa and T3 Code MCP names are no longer needed in any list; drop the code that builds them if nothing else uses it, and keep the role text that tells the librarians to search with the Exa tools.

Determine the built-in tool names to deny from the role capabilities and the documented tool names above plus any built-in the current lists name; derive the denylist in code from one list of built-ins so a role's grant and denial cannot drift. Add a test asserting: no generated agent has a `tools:` line; every agent's disallowedTools contains WebSearch and WebFetch and no `mcp__` entry; each role's effective built-ins (all built-ins minus its denylist) equal its previous allowlist's built-ins, except WebSearch/WebFetch.
